title: Flatness detection under finite clopen restriction
statement: Flatness detection under finite clopen restriction.

source.place: Tag 03ER (3), with the clopen exactness and zero-insertion argument.

proof.text: Reindex the finite index type by Fin(card I), using Fintype.ofFinite and Fintype.equivFin. Disjointness and the covering property transport along this equivalence. This permits the gluing theorem to be instantiated without adding the original index universe to the module universe.

The explicit site tensor functor is naturally isomorphic to monoidal tensorRight by SheafOfModules.siteSheafTensorRightIso. Tensoring preserves finite colimits by the existing cochain tensor instance. Consequently IsFlatOnSite F is equivalent to preservation of finite limits by tensorRight F.

Apply clopen_ringed_module_gluing to the underlying ring sheaf. Its restriction functor and the supplied inverse, unit and counit form an equivalence. It supplies zero insertions e_i with e_i followed by restriction r_i naturally isomorphic to the identity, and zero restrictions off the diagonal. Restriction preserves finite limits: the module-sheaf forgetful functor followed by the additive-presheaf forgetful functor reflects limits, and after this composition restriction is precomposition of additive presheaves.

Apply clopen_structural_data to get the braided structures on the restriction functors and the adjunction r_i left adjoint to each zero insertion e_i supplied by gluing. Thus e_i preserves limits. Functor.Monoidal.commTensorRight identifies r_i followed by tensorRight(r_i F) with tensorRight F followed by r_i.

If tensorRight F preserves finite limits, then so does e_i followed by tensorRight F followed by r_i. Whisker the tensor comparison by e_i and compose with e_i followed by r_i isomorphic to the identity, obtaining a natural isomorphism from tensorRight(r_i F) to that composite. Preservation of finite limits transports across this isomorphism, proving component flatness.

Conversely suppose every component tensor functor preserves finite limits. Each composite tensorRight F followed by r_i preserves them, by the tensor comparison and preservation by r_i. For any finite diagram and limiting cone, assemble the coordinate lifts of the image cones into a lift in the product category; its factorization and uniqueness hold coordinatewise. The gluing equivalence reflects that image limit, so tensorRight F preserves finite limits. Translate back to IsFlatOnSite and transport the universal component assertion along the finite-index equivalence. This argument needs no nonempty-index or nonzero-ring assumption.

lean.statement:
theorem clopen_flat_detection
    (X : Scheme.{t}) (I : Type w) [Finite I] (Y : I → Scheme.{t})
    (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ X) [∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i)] [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (j i)]
    (hdisjoint : Pairwise (fun i k ↦ Disjoint (Set.range (j i)) (Set.range (j k))))
    (hcover : ∀ x : X, ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (j i))
    (R : Sheaf (topology X) CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)}) :
    ∀ F : ClopenData.clopenTensorModules.{t, u} R,
      SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := topology X) (R := R) F ↔
        ∀ i, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := topology (Y i))
          (R := (ClopenData.clopenTensorRings.{t, u} (j i)).obj R)
          ((ClopenData.clopenTensorRestriction.{t, u} (j i) R).obj F)
